etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English opake, from Latin opacus (“shaded, shady, dark”) (of unknown origin), later reinforced from Middle French opaque. Doublet of ubac.
senses: Allowing little light to pass through, not translucent or transparent.
(obsolete, poetic) An area of darkness; a place or region with no light.
Something which is opaque rather than translucent.
